identities.notes: Any keyboard exposing QMK's raw HID collection FF60:0061 (Keychron Q/V/K Pro, most VIA-supported boards). The name shown is the USB product string. UDB checks that the board speaks VIA (command 01) before anything else.

use.purpose: QMK raw HID: VIA commands as 32-byte output reports, replies as 32-byte input reports, no report ID

linux.notes: Needs a udev rule giving the user access to the keyboard's hidraw node (as VIA documents)

limitations: Wired only. Raw HID over Bluetooth or a 2.4 GHz receiver is not documented.
Lighting needs VIA protocol 12 or 13 (QMK 0.19 or newer). Older firmware and Vial (protocol 9) get the handshake and layer count only.
Effect numbers depend on the effects the firmware was built with. Without the board's VIA definition, UDB shows them as numbers.
Brightness is rescaled to the board's own maximum, so the value read back can differ slightly from the one written.
Keymap and macro editing need the board's matrix size from its VIA definition and are not implemented yet.
Keyboard-specific custom values (channel 0, e.g. Keychron's settings) are refused.
UDB never sends the bootloader, EEPROM-reset or keymap-reset commands.

evidence.source: QMK quantum/via.c (commit 7a1bbf37): via_qmk_{backlight,rgblight,rgb_matrix,led_matrix}_{get,set}_value; value ID 1 on channels 1, 2, 3 and 5

features.notes: Per lighting channel the firmware has: backlight, rgblight, RGB matrix or LED matrix.
